Runs one timed agent turn-loop: parses fenced tool calls, executes them against a sandboxed shell and jailed filesystem, and captures a JSONL transcript, all under a deadline.
Keeps the soup's pointers at the blueprint fresh and records what each design-and-build cycle changed — detecting and reporting divergence, and never writing anything blueprint-side.

Owns the round: it decides whether a coordinator may wake at all, opens the round against one frozen context, collects the plan, hands it to the runner, and runs the fixed close order of leakage screen, terminal wake, then curation.
Executes any conforming plan graph: it validates the specification, dispatches each node as a scoped child, branches on declared exit states, and resumes a crashed run at the first incomplete node.
Owns the captured market corpus and every dataset split declared over it: capture with verified hashes, the stratified holdout carve, and the seal that is set once and never unset.

Manages a branch-per-build sandbox repo (`mindcode`): seeds it, cuts a branch per iteration, gates and builds a builder's commit, runs its train/eval/holdout windows with the holdout sealed off, and tears down after every run.
Runs chat-completion generation behind one contract, over two interchangeable backends: local Gemma on Metal and headless claude-cli.
Declares the shared LLM-inference and experiment-loop wire shapes (`inference_api`, `experiment_protocol`) that other researchd components build and call against.
Screens every closed round for data leakage before anything from it is curated, files what it finds, quarantines what was touched, and authors the guardrails that come out of it.
Reads Binance monthly 1m kline archives and hands bars out one at a time, structurally forbidding any lookahead past the reader's position.

Turns the one soup into many indexes: it owns the projection registry, the mechanistic renderers that enforce the fences, snapshot freezing and hashing, and the ladder-level history the future buoyancy estimator will train on.

Runs one backtest episode — a strategy against a declared dataset window under a configuration — and writes its metrics mechanically, refusing any episode whose experiment was not pre-registered before a sealed number could exist.
Owns the soup itself: every node, edge and tool-call row, the id sequences, the prose bodies, and the validating write transaction that makes an illegal write unsayable.
A read-only local view over the soup: the coordinators, the rounds they ran, the episodes and their metrics, the champion boards, and the leakage and guardrail history.
